thread.title: Why Other FAANG Stocks Could Drop

author: Evie Liu
title: Why Other FAANG Stocks Could Drop
text:
By Evie Liu July 26, 2018 12:07 p.m. ET There are two major schools of thought of how to view rising stock valuations: value and momentum.
Value investors, who believe in finding undervalued stocks and buying at low prices ahead of a rebound, could see outperformance as a sign of a downtrend to come. Momentum investors, on the other hand, believe in the continuance of existing trends–the so-called "momentum"–and therefore bet on the stocks that have been surging.
Over the past two years, the market has seemed to favor the momentum strategy. Investors have been pouring money into the most expensive stocks when risks arise, and view them as safe havens during turbulent times.
Some more evidence of momentum's pull: The price/earnings valuation spread between momentum and value stocks has been surging to new highs, and the spread is most elevated in the tech and consumer-discretionary sectors, notes Chris Senyek of Wolfe Research .
"Our strong sense is that the risk-reward in high momentum stocks is highly skewed to the downside," wrote Senyek in a report published last Friday. He expects there'll be a sharp rotation out of momentum stocks if trade tensions are resolved without drama .
If a trade war does unfold , however, the broader market will likely experience a downturn and momentum names with the highest P/E valuation might materially underperform.
He recommends investors to reduce positions in momentum stocks such as the FAANGs— Facebook (FB), Amazon.com (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), Netflix (NFLX), and Alphabet (GOOGL)—and invest proceeds in other sectors in the weeks to come. Facebook has already plunged on a disappointing quarter and outlook.
